answer: The spiral detector writes to umber, and mirror shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 57 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 102 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 18 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
